Why This Is Asked

This question probes end-to-end debugging skills for cross-namespace aliasing, gateway routing, and identity in a Consul Connect mesh, especially under load and after a new alias introduction.

- Consul service aliasing across namespaces
- Mesh gateway routing and policy configuration
- SPIFFE identity propagation and mTLS
- Telemetry: Envoy logs, Consul DNS, and health checks

```bash
# Discover services and aliases
consul catalog services
# DNS validation for alias

# Inspect gateway routes/policies

# Check service identity and certificates
consul tls ca list
# Monitor Envoy logs for connection issues
kubectl logs -n <namespace> -l app=envoy -c envoy
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates understanding of namespace isolation, ACL policy management, and secure service-to-service communication patterns in hybrid Kubernetes/VM environments.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped ACL policies for environment segregation
- Service identities and intentions for zero-trust networking
- Token lifecycle management with automatic rotation
- Vault integration for PKI and credential management
- Blue-green deployment patterns for safe service promotion

## Code Example
```hcl
# Consul ACL Policy (HCL)
node_prefix "" {
  policy = "read"
}

service "" {
  policy = "write"
}

# Service-specific permissions
service "pricing" {
  policy = "read"
}
```

## Implementation Notes
- Use namespace prefixes to enforce environment boundaries
- Implement token TTLs of 24-72 hours for security
- Configure intentions with default-deny posture
- Leverage Vault for automated certificate management
